::: {.remark .notes}

We use uppercase letters ($X$, $Y$, $Z$, ...) for random variables,
and lowercase letters ($x$, $y$, $z$, ...) for their realized (observed) values.
We write $\{X = x\}$ for the event $\{\outcome \in \samplespace : X(\outcome) = x\}$,
and similarly for $\{X \le x\}$ and other conditions on $X$.
A fully rigorous definition also requires the function to be *measurable*,
so that every such set is an event with a probability;
that requirement never binds in these notes.

:::
